newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat closes lower on slack exports.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat closes lower on slack exports.

text.p: MGE spring wheat closed lower on slow exports of U.S. spring wheat, traders said.
"Export business is slowing down, at least for us (spring wheat) it is," a trader said.

Pressure also came from end-of-the-week position squaring after Thursday's rally that was tied to a surge in CBOT corn and soybean futures. Corn and soy traded lower in early dealings Friday but corn staged a recovery into the close and ended higher.

Traders said the results of a tour this week of key U.S. spring wheat areas were supportive to the market but not surprising. "I think the tour estimate of 31.3 (bushels per acre) is in the market now," a trader said.

The tour of dark northern spring wheat and durum areas of the U.S. pegged 1997 U.S. spring wheat yields at 31.3 bushels per acre, below the 36.4 estimated by the tour in 1996. Durum yields were estimated by the tour group at 27.7 bushels per acre, below the 29.7 bushels forecast during last year's tour.
News the EU would begin an export tax on the EU's wheat exports may have helped underpin the market, sources said.
MGE spring wheat futures closed unchanged to 2-1/2 cents lower, with September down 1-1/2 at $3.91-1/2.
MGE feed barley closed unchanged with September steady at $6.20 per cwt.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the MGE at 14,303 contracts, below the 21,434 traded Thursday.
